title: Can You Get Your Florida Real Estate License Completely Online?
metaDesc: Can you get your Florida real estate license completely online? Mostly: the course is online, but fingerprinting and the state exam are still in person.
h1: Can You Get Your Florida Real Estate License Completely Online?
about: Whether Florida's real estate pre-license process can be completed entirely online

hub.name: Become a Real Estate Agent in Florida

answer: Mostly, but not completely. Florida’s 63-hour pre-license course is widely available fully online and self-paced, and you submit your application online too. But fingerprinting typically requires an in-person Livescan appointment, and the state licensing exam is administered at an in-person testing center, not online.
takeaways: The required 63-hour Florida pre-license course is available fully online through state-approved providers.
Fingerprinting for your background check typically requires an in-person Livescan appointment; there’s no remote option.
The state real estate exam is administered at an approved in-person testing center, not online or via remote proctoring.
Passing the exam leaves you with an inactive license until a sponsoring broker activates it.
Knowing the two in-person steps upfront helps you plan a realistic timeline instead of getting caught off guard.
tldr: You can complete Florida's 63-hour pre-license course, and your application, fully online. But fingerprinting requires an in-person Livescan appointment and the state exam is given at an in-person testing center, so the process is mostly, not completely, online.
body:
Can you take Florida's pre-license course entirely online?

Yes. The 63-hour Florida real estate sales associate pre-license course is one of the most flexible parts of the whole process. Several state-approved providers offer it fully online, self-paced, so you can study around a job, kids, or a second career. You watch or read the material, work through practice questions, and finish on your own schedule instead of sitting in a classroom two nights a week. Some providers also offer live, instructor-led online sessions if you prefer a set schedule and real-time interaction over pure self-paced study; either format satisfies the state's course requirement.

Is the whole licensing process online, though?

Mostly, but not entirely. The course itself is online. Submitting your application to the state is online. Two important steps are not: fingerprinting and the state licensing exam. Anyone telling you the entire path from zero to licensed happens on a laptop is skipping over those two requirements, and they matter for planning your timeline and your calendar around work or family commitments.

Where do fingerprints and the background check happen?

Florida requires an electronic fingerprint (Livescan) appointment at an approved location as part of your application. This is done in person, there’s no remote or mail-in option, and the results feed into a state and federal background check. Most candidates schedule this near the start of the process, since it can take time to clear and you’ll want it done before you’re ready to sit for the exam. Waiting until the last minute is the most common way this step delays an otherwise-fast timeline.

Can you take the state exam online?

No. The Florida real estate sales associate exam is administered at an approved in-person testing center. You’ll schedule a seat, bring valid ID, and complete the exam under proctored conditions on-site. There’s currently no remote-proctoring or at-home option for this step, so budget travel time to a testing location, and check seat availability early since popular locations and time slots can book up.

Does the online course provider you pick matter?

All approved providers cover the same state-mandated curriculum, since the content is set by Florida requirements, not by the school. What differs is format (self-paced versus scheduled live sessions), price, and how much practice-exam support and instructor access is included. It’s worth comparing a couple of state-approved options for format and support rather than assuming they’re all identical, but no online course, however good, changes the fact that fingerprinting and the exam still happen in person.

So what does the realistic timeline look like?

Roughly: finish the 63-hour online course at your own pace (this varies widely by person, from a couple of weeks of focused study to a couple of months part-time), schedule and complete your Livescan fingerprinting, submit your application to the state, then schedule and pass the in-person exam. Processing and scheduling windows shift over time, so always confirm current timing directly with the state and your course provider rather than assuming a fixed number of days or weeks.

What do you need after you pass the exam?

Passing the exam doesn’t make you an active agent on its own. You’ll hold an inactive license until you affiliate with a sponsoring broker, who activates it with the state. This is the step where your choice of brokerage starts to matter far more than which online course you picked: the training, mentorship, lead support, and culture you join shapes how your first year in the business actually goes.

Why does "mostly online" trip people up?

Because course marketing understandably emphasizes the online, self-paced part, since that’s the flexible, appealing piece. But candidates who assume literally everything happens from home sometimes get caught off guard scrambling to book a fingerprinting appointment or a testing center seat close to a deadline, sometimes right before a planned career start date. Knowing upfront that two in-person steps are built into Florida’s process lets you plan around work, childcare, or a move, instead of discovering it last minute and losing weeks to scheduling.

Once you're licensed, the online-versus-in-person question behind you, the decision that actually shapes your career is which brokerage you join. Course formats, fingerprinting procedures, and exam scheduling can change; confirm current requirements with the Florida DBPR and your course provider. Educational only, not legal advice.

faq.q: Can I really finish the Florida real estate course without leaving my house?
faq.a: Yes, the 63-hour pre-license course itself can be completed fully online through a state-approved provider, either self-paced or through scheduled live online sessions.

faq.q: Do I have to go somewhere in person to get fingerprinted?
faq.a: Yes. Florida requires an electronic Livescan fingerprinting appointment at an approved location as part of your application; there's no remote or mail-in option for this step.

faq.q: Is the Florida real estate exam offered online or remotely?
faq.a: No. The state exam is administered at an approved in-person testing center under proctored conditions. There's currently no remote-proctoring or at-home option.

faq.q: Once I pass the exam, am I automatically an active agent?
faq.a: No. You'll hold an inactive license until you affiliate with a sponsoring broker, who activates it with the state so you can begin practicing.
